answer: The paper's ITL formula ITL = a/(1 - b*lambda) fits BLIS well across 5-130 req/s: R²=0.956 for always-disaggregate (AD) and R²=0.927 for always-local (AL). AD consistently produces lower ITL than AL at every rate, with the gap growing monotonically from 0.06 ms (rate=5) to 1.68 ms (rate=130), driven by the 1/(1-rho) queueing amplifier removing prefill work from decode servers. Conversely, AD carries a TTFT penalty of 4-10 ms over AL due to KV-transfer overhead, narrowing under load as AL TTFT degrades faster. The formula begins to underpredict AL ITL above ~100 req/s (AL R²=0.927 vs AD R²=0.956) because mixed prefill+decode batches introduce non-linearities not captured by the single-server M/G/1 approximation. The fitted b_AL/b_AD = 1.21, implying AL carries ~21% more effective work per request than AD decode servers, consistent with the theoretical W_P/W_D ratio for 512-token prompts and 128-token outputs.
